Now we are merging two PDDL domains into one domain. Please help judge whether two PDDL operators are equivalent.

domain_1:
    action in domain_1: (:action rich_brother_attempt_to_move_stone :parameters (?rich - entity ?stone - item ?loc - location) :precondition (and (stone_at ?stone ?loc) (state ?rich)) :effect (and (stone_moved ?stone) (woe_on_shoulder bitter_woe ?rich) (not (stone_at ?stone ?loc))))
    predicates explaination in domain_1: {'(state ?e - entity)': "entity ?e is in the state 'state'; used as precondition of request_help_from_rich_brother, precondition of rich_brother_attempt_to_move_stone", '(stone_at ?s - item ?l - location)': "relation 'stone at' holds; arguments: ?s is a item, ?l is a location; used as precondition of move_heavy_stone, effect of move_heavy_stone, precondition of hide_woe_under_stone, effect of hide_woe_under_stone, precondition of rich_brother_attempt_to_move_stone, effect of rich_brother_attempt_to_move_stone", '(stone_moved ?s - item)': "item ?s is in the state 'stone moved'; used as effect of move_heavy_stone, effect of hide_woe_under_stone, effect of rich_brother_attempt_to_move_stone", '(woe_on_shoulder ?monster - entity ?carrier - entity)': "relation 'woe on shoulder' holds; arguments: ?monster is a entity, ?carrier is a entity; used as effect of allow_woe_to_ride_on_shoulder, precondition of hide_woe_under_stone, effect of hide_woe_under_stone, effect of rich_brother_attempt_to_move_stone, precondition of accept_woe_as_burden"}

domain_2:
    action in domain_2: (:action show_kettle_to_friend :parameters (?f ?t - entity ?k - item) :precondition (has ?t ?k) :effect (has ?f ?k))
    predicates explaination in domain_2: {'(has ?e - entity ?i - item)': "relation 'has' holds; arguments: ?e is a entity, ?i is a item; used as precondition of hang_kettle, precondition of sell_kettle_to_tinker, effect of sell_kettle_to_tinker, precondition of kettle_transform_to_fur_badger, precondition of show_kettle_to_friend, effect of show_kettle_to_friend, precondition of arrange_exhibition, precondition of perform_show"}

Please judge whether the two operators can be merged into one action based on following rules:
(1) If the two actions have the same name, they MUST be merged into one action;
(2) If the two actions are semantically equivalent (although they may differ in preconditions and effects), merge them. Genrally, you need to union their preconditions and effects.
(3) Note that do NOT merge two actions if the logic becomes more complex after merging. For example, do NOT use "or", "when" to union two actions (about their preconditions and effects). Namely NOT too general. 
(4) Do NOT invent any predicate.
(5) If you decide to merge two actions. You can invent new action name. But the new name must be reasonable according to the whole predicates in the action.
    For example: if the action expresses the meaning of "pick some object from drawer" according to the predicates in preconditions and effects, just name it like "pick_from_drawer", instead of "pick_from_container", etc.
(6) Keep the given PDDL style. Please use PDDL 1.0 and do NOT use Conditional Effects like "when", etc.
(7) Note the number of brackets in the PDDL format.

Your output should include four part:
(1) reasoning: your analysis process;
(2) merge_flag: whether the two operators can be merged into one;
(3) new_operator_name: if equivalent, output the new operator name (in one of the given operator or a new invented operator).
(4) new_operator: if equivalent, output the new operator in PDDL format.

If "merge_flag" is false, the "new_operator_name" and "new_operator" parts are null.

Your output should be in JSON format like below:
{
    "reasoning": "your analysis process",
    "merge_flag": true,
    "new_operator_name": "open_door",
    "new_operator": "(:action open_door \n :parameters (?r ?d) \n :precondition (and (hand_free ?r)) \n :effect (and (is_open ?d)))"
}

Do NOT output any strange symbols like "\".

The effect is that the stone is moved and the rich brother has a 'woe' on his shoulder.
